newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BLACKBURN, SOUTHAMPTON EDGE TOWARDS SAFETY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BLACKBURN, SOUTHAMPTON EDGE TOWARDS SAFETY.

text.p: Blackburn and Southampton boosted their chances of premier league survival on Tuesday with vital victories in difficult circumstances.
Blackburn beat UEFA Cup hopefuls Sheffield Wednesday 4-1 at Ewood Park -- a result which should ensure them top flight soccer next season.
Southampton went to Sunderland, also battling to stay in the top flight, and came away with a 1-0 victory.
In the night's other matches Chelsea beat Wimbledon 1-0 in a re-run of their F.A. Cup semifinal earlier this month while Leeds and Aston Villa drew 0-0.
Blackburn, the 1995 English champions, took a 3-0 lead by halftime thanks to goals from Norway's Henning Berg, England wing-back Graeme Le Saux and captain Tim Sherwood.
Gary Flitcroft added a fourth after the interval and, although Wednesday pulled back a goal from the penalty spot through Italian Benito Carbone, Blackburn never looked like losing.
Norwegian Egil Ostenstad scored Southampton's vital goal at Sunderland to take Southampton into 15th place in the 20-side table.
Sunderland drop to 17th, just two points above the relegation zone.
